# RFC 1 §12 test vectors.
#
# Flat and line-oriented on purpose: the audience is a second
# implementation, which needs no CBOR parser to read this.
# Format: <name> <space> <hex or decimal>
#
# Generated by apps/krab-tui/src/vectors.rs and checked on every test
# run. RFC 1 §12 requires two independent implementations to agree
# before RFC 1 reaches Final; there is currently one.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# CHECKABLE BY INSPECTION
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Every derived value is printed together with the inputs it was
# derived from, so a reader holding RFC 1 can confirm the derivation
# with a hash utility and no Krab code at all. That is the point: an
# output on its own is only checkable by rebuilding the thing that
# produced it, which is what a second implementation is for and what
# this file cannot substitute for.
#
# What it *can* catch is the class of error that does not need a
# second reader to find: a swapped concatenation order, the wrong
# endianness on an epoch, a label off by a byte, an output length
# taken from the wrong line of the spec. Those are visible here.
#
# Each block says what agreement with it is worth:
#
#   anchor: external    values computed outside this codebase, with a
#                       different implementation of the primitive.
#                       Agreement is evidence of correctness.
#   anchor: derivable   recomputable by hand from the inputs printed
#                       above them, using only the named standard
#                       primitives. Agreement is evidence the
#                       construction is what the RFC describes.
#   anchor: drift       self-consistency only. Agreement means this
#                       implementation has not changed. It is NOT
#                       evidence that it is right.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# PRIMITIVES, NAMED
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
#
# RFC 1 §6.2 writes "HKDF-Expand" and never names a hash, which
# taken alone is not implementable interoperably. §6.1 pins the
# suite's KDF, and this file follows that reading. The wrong
# inference is the natural one — every other digest in Krab is
# BLAKE3 — so it is stated here rather than left to be guessed:
#
#   object identifiers (§4)   BLAKE3-256
#   tag derivation (§6.2)     HKDF-SHA256, Expand ONLY, no Extract
#   agreement                 X25519 (RFC 7748), static-static
#   AEAD (§6.1)               ChaCha20-Poly1305
#
# The absent Extract is deliberate and is RFC 1 §6.2 as frozen: the
# PRK fed to Expand is a raw X25519 output, or for inbox mode a raw
# public key. See CRYPTO-REVIEW.md §3. An implementation that adds
# Extract produces different tags for every object and shares mail
# with nobody, silently.

## bucket boundaries (§8.1)
# anchor: derivable — arithmetic on the published ladder.
# bucket.for.N is the smallest bucket admitting N bytes INCLUDING the
# 16-byte routing header; `none` means N exceeds the largest bucket.
bucket.0.bytes 256
bucket.for.256 0
bucket.for.257 1
bucket.1.bytes 1024
bucket.for.1024 1
bucket.for.1025 2
bucket.2.bytes 4096
bucket.for.4096 2
bucket.for.4097 3
bucket.3.bytes 16384
bucket.for.16384 3
bucket.for.16385 4
bucket.4.bytes 65536
bucket.for.65536 4
bucket.for.65537 5
bucket.5.bytes 262144
bucket.for.262144 5
bucket.for.262145 none

## canonical encoding and identifiers (§4)
# anchor: derivable — id = BLAKE3-256(domain.object ‖ object.bytes).
# The whole preimage is printed, so no Krab code is needed to check it.
#
# The header is 16 bytes: version(1), class(1), size_bucket(1),
# flags(1), expiry_min(4) as u32 LITTLE-endian, tag(8). The four
# single bytes have no byte order; the only multi-byte field is the
# expiry, and it is little-endian — same as the epoch inside a tag's
# info string, which is the one consistency worth stating out loud.
#
# 29766240 is 0x01C63260, so bytes 4..8 read 6032c601. An earlier
# revision of this comment said big-endian; the checker in this
# directory disagreed with it, which is the entire point of printing
# the field values next to the encoding.
# The object is header ‖ body ‖ zero padding to the bucket size, and
# the identifier covers the padding — which is why RFC 1 §8.1 fixes
# padding at zero. `id_with_dirty_padding` is the same object with its
# final byte set to 1, and is a different identifier.
domain.object.hex 6b7261622f6f626a2f7631
domain.object.ascii krab/obj/v1
header.class0.encoded 010000006032c6011122334455667788
header.class0.version 1
header.class0.class 0
header.class0.size_bucket 0
header.class0.flags 0
header.class0.expiry_min 29766240
header.class0.tag 1122334455667788
object.class0.body abababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababab
object.class0.len 256
object.class0.bytes 
object.class0.id 62ddc3ea64df0593b7d347731e55bc976b4355376d76e6b530a936031318b178
object.class0.bytes_with_dirty_padding 
object.class0.id_with_dirty_padding 974983b94f1f3b1262bbe65a10b52b9a1d2be8c995f49cc8d9d8c00665b8d211
header.class1.encoded 010100006032c6011122334455667788
header.class1.version 1
header.class1.class 1
header.class1.size_bucket 0
header.class1.flags 0
header.class1.expiry_min 29766240
header.class1.tag 1122334455667788
object.class1.body abababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababab
object.class1.len 256
object.class1.bytes 
object.class1.id 5e38550edee16237de93637c05f85a69295856782f878e345a97ad4194208c99
object.class1.bytes_with_dirty_padding 
object.class1.id_with_dirty_padding 61d20b9a71bec2a99f1cfe211a0c7187eb33ae4dbcaf124225e44ecf2c543794

## HKDF-Expand construction, fixed PRK (§6.2)
# anchor: external — these six outputs were computed outside this
# codebase, with a separate HMAC implementation, before being
# committed. A second implementation can check them with nothing but
# HMAC-SHA256: no X25519, no clamping, no shared assumptions.
#
#   tag = HKDF-Expand(prk, info, L)
#   info = label ‖ u32_le(epoch)
#   L    = 8
#
# NO Extract step. The PRK is used as the HMAC key directly.
# The epoch is LITTLE-endian: RFC 1 §6.2 writes u32(epoch) and RFC 2
# §4.1 writes u32_le(epoch); the explicit one governs. Epoch 20670 is
# 0x50BE, so the info tail reads be500000 and not 000050be — which is
# the one byte-order error this file exists to make visible.
#
# The info bytes are printed in full below. Read them against §6.2 and
# the concatenation order is checkable by eye.
kdf.hash SHA-256
kdf.L 8
kdf.extract none
label.tag.hex 6b7261622f7461672f7631
label.tag.ascii krab/tag/v1
label.inbox.hex 6b7261622f696e626f782f7631
label.inbox.ascii krab/inbox/v1
kdf.prk 4242424242424242424242424242424242424242424242424242424242424242
kdf.info.pairwise.20670 6b7261622f7461672f7631be500000
kdf.pairwise.20670 9df7b6895987ed3c
kdf.info.inbox.20670 6b7261622f696e626f782f7631be500000
kdf.inbox.20670 684f0e4dde844750
kdf.info.pairwise.20671 6b7261622f7461672f7631bf500000
kdf.pairwise.20671 2daceced91f7148c
kdf.info.inbox.20671 6b7261622f696e626f782f7631bf500000
kdf.inbox.20671 249743bc3eadc595
kdf.info.pairwise.20672 6b7261622f7461672f7631c0500000
kdf.pairwise.20672 77f7856b7dbebdea
kdf.info.inbox.20672 6b7261622f696e626f782f7631c0500000
kdf.inbox.20672 b4296a826dba95f8

## tag derivation across an epoch boundary (§6.2)
# anchor: derivable — every input is printed, including both private
# keys and the agreed secret, so this needs no Krab code to check:
#
#   kx.shared        = X25519(kx.a.secret, kx.b.public)
#                    = X25519(kx.b.secret, kx.a.public)   (symmetric)
#   tag.pairwise.E   = HKDF-Expand(kx.shared,  label.tag   ‖ u32_le(E), 8)
#   tag.inbox.E      = HKDF-Expand(kx.b.public, label.inbox ‖ u32_le(E), 8)
#
# Note what the second line says: the inbox PRK is the recipient's
# PUBLIC KEY, used verbatim as an HMAC key. That is RFC 1 §6.2 as
# frozen, and it is why anyone holding the public key can compute the
# tag — which is what makes first contact possible and what makes
# messages to an inbox tag linkable within an epoch (RFC 2 §4.2).
#
# The private keys are printed because these are test vectors and
# publishing them is what makes the block checkable. They are
# generated from a counter and protect nothing.
#
# Once kx.shared is confirmed against RFC 7748, the two tag lines
# reduce to the fixed-PRK block above, which is externally anchored.
kx.a.secret cf5ee9a0494aa9613e05d5ed725b804b12f4a465ee635acc3a311de8740489ea
kx.a.public 05d04a3dbe6729b7a23ca50b4f56a4be55cfce3f059f367fe51ecea0686c5c38
kx.b.secret 790877ccb0aef7f965ad818cab2e16220d2bbebda08d296c2533f823c8e4b0ed
kx.b.public 76b8fcca5fe5eb4faf05030df0c6774f1fb17cb277d1e85c26871be07420280f
kx.shared 2a15f93ba3076e8c63f079217e27378207d8541db0966eb7b93f696351c5b416
kx.inbox_prk_is kx.b.public — the recipient's public key, used as the PRK
tag.pairwise.20670 d39db2302396f08b
tag.inbox.20670 f73e1adae4248b71
tag.pairwise.20671 5060a67e42cb4e02
tag.inbox.20671 e2d9c85bbe5e4bb1
tag.pairwise.20672 441b96475d805fc0
tag.inbox.20672 03553d784f2b7c8e

## AAD construction (§6.1)
# anchor: derivable — the inputs are printed, so the concatenation and
# the CBOR map are both checkable:
#
#   aad.prefix = deterministic CBOR map, keys ascending, definite
#                lengths:  {0: epoch, 1: tag_mode, 2: suite, 4: enc}
#   aad.full   = aad.header ‖ aad.prefix
#
# **Key 5 (the ciphertext) is omitted, and key 3 (admission) is absent
# entirely** — RFC 1 §4.2. A map with either present is a different
# AAD and every open fails.
#
# Key 4 is *included*, so the AAD cannot be built before the KEM has
# run. That is what makes §6.1's claim true that the AAD binds epoch
# and suite as well as expiry, tag and class — the header alone binds
# only the last three.
#
# info.classN is the HPKE info string: "krab/v1/" ‖ one byte of
# class. Not part of the AAD; printed here because §6.1 fixes it and
# a wrong one fails to open with no other symptom.
aad.header 010001006032c6010909090909090909
aad.env.epoch 20671
aad.env.tag_mode 0
aad.env.suite 1
aad.env.enc 5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a
aad.env.ciphertext_is_omitted 1
aad.env.admission_is_absent 1
aad.prefix a4001950bf010002010458205a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a
aad.full 010001006032c6010909090909090909a4001950bf010002010458205a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5a
info.prefix.hex 6b7261622f76312f
info.prefix.ascii krab/v1/
info.class0 6b7261622f76312f00
info.class1 6b7261622f76312f01

## seal and open (§6)
# anchor: drift — HPKE is randomised, so a ciphertext is not a fixed
# value and cannot be. What is pinned is the SHAPE: the lengths, the
# mode, the suite, and that a round trip through the wire form
# recovers the plaintext.
#
# A second implementation checks these by producing its own sealed
# object and comparing the numbers, not by reproducing these bytes.
# mode_auth is used for a known correspondent; mode_base for first
# contact, where the recipient does not yet hold the sender's static
# key and so cannot decapsulate in auth mode (RFC 2 §4.2).
mode_auth.object.len 256
mode_auth.bucket 0
mode_auth.tag_mode 0
mode_auth.suite 1
mode_auth.enc.len 32
mode_auth.ciphertext.len 32
mode_auth.plaintext.len 16
mode_auth.body_size_for 88
mode_base.object.len 256
mode_base.bucket 0
mode_base.tag_mode 1
mode_base.suite 1
mode_base.enc.len 32
mode_base.ciphertext.len 32
mode_base.plaintext.len 16
mode_base.body_size_for 88

## rejection cases (§11)
# anchor: drift — each line names the refusal an implementation must
# produce for that input. The NAMES are the checkable part: two
# implementations agreeing that a case is rejected, but for different
# reasons, have not agreed about §11.
reject.id_mismatch IdMismatch
reject.bad_length BadPadding
reject.expired Expired
reject.too_far_future TooFarFuture
reject.duplicate Duplicate
reject.bad_class Unrecognised
reject.reserved_flag_set Malformed
reject.nonzero_padding BadPadding
reject.body_not_cbor BadBody
reject.reserved_body_key BadBody

## forward compatibility (§10)
# anchor: an unknown `ver` is CARRIED, not refused. §10: "a relay
# encountering `ver` it does not know MUST route, filter, and expire
# from the 16-byte routing header alone, and MUST store and forward
# the remaining bytes opaquely." An implementation that rejects here
# partitions the network at the first protocol revision.
forward.unknown_version carried
forward.unknown_version_id_mismatch IdMismatch
forward.unknown_version_expired Expired
forward.unknown_version_bad_length BadPadding
